title: The for Loop
objective: Use a for loop to repeat code a known number of times.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only; the conditional half of this book chapter is covered in Code Forge's Control Flow chapter. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A for loop packs three parts into one line: a starting value, a condition that keeps the loop going, and an update that runs after each pass. for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { ... } starts i at 0, keeps looping while i < n, and increases i by 1 after every pass.
The three parts run in a fixed order: the starting value runs once, then before each pass the condition is checked, and after each pass the update runs. i++ is shorthand for i = i + 1.

Reach for a for loop when you already know how many times you want to repeat something — counting up to a number, or visiting each position in a fixed-length sequence — instead of a while loop's open-ended condition.
explanation.rule: for (start; condition; update) { ... } runs start once, then repeats while condition is true, running update after every pass.

examples.title: Counting Up
examples.note: i starts at 1, the loop keeps going while i <= 5, and i increases by 1 after each pass — so this logs 1 through 5.

checks.question: for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { console.log(i); } — what does this log?

feedback.correct: Correct — i starts at 0 and the loop stops once i is no longer less than 3, so the last value logged is 2.
feedback.incorrect: i starts at 0, and the loop keeps going only while i < 3 — so it stops before logging 3.

assignment.title: Multiples Table
assignment.brief: Write printMultiples(n) that logs n multiplied by 1 through 5, one per line, using a for loop.
requirements: Use a for loop that runs exactly 5 times.
Log n * i for i from 1 through 5, one value per line.

hints: The for loop's three parts are: let i = 1, i <= 5, and i++.
Multiply n by i inside the loop body.
console.log(n * i) each pass, do not build a single combined string.
